summary: Count retained agent-message sends for the usage estimate in background pages after an upgrade, not on the first usage read

replay.detail: No claim or shared projection replay. The local agent_message_sends and agent_message_days counts are rebuilt from retained message.sent claims, as before; only when and in what steps changes.

schema.detail: No table, index or schema-version change. While the backfill runs, a meta row (agent_message_days_v1_through) holds the store_index it has counted through; it is removed when the counts are ready.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules, retention or digest change. Earliest-send arbitration and test/probe exclusion are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: The /v1/client/usage response is unchanged and never shows partial counts: a usage read that arrives before the backfill finishes completes the rest inline, as every first read did before.

downtime.detail: Opening the store still does no backfill. On the first start after an upgrade, the daemon counts sends in pages of at most 500 message.sent claims, one background writer turn each and 100 ms apart. On the load test's busy-host store (4,947 messages) the whole backfill took 205 ms in one writer transaction, about 41 us a send, so a page holds the writer for about 20 ms. The first usage read there took 212 ms before this change and about 10 ms after the pages finish.

manual.detail: No manual step. The backfill starts with the daemon and resumes from its cursor after a restart.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back is supported: an earlier build ignores the cursor row and, if the counts are not ready, rebuilds them on its first estimate as it did before.
